classification.difficultyReason: Translate the next financial year to Year11, draw and extend a reasonable trend line, read and round monetary units and distinguish extrapolation from interpolation.

inlines.text: Consider the time series below, showing a company’s profit for consecutive financial years over a 10 year period. ‘Year 1’ marks the financial year 1988–1989, ‘Year 2’ marks the financial year 1989–1990, and so on. ‘Year 10’ marks the financial year 1997–1998.
Create a line of best fit on the time series and use it to predict the company’s profits, to the nearest $100 000, in the financial year 1998–1999.
(Predicting future values in a time series based on previously observed values is called
.) Is your answer an example of interpolation or extrapolation?

spec.description: Ten observed profits joined consecutively; horizontal gridlines every 0.5 million, no vertical gridlines, and plotting space through Year 12. Coordinates reconstruct graphical positions and are not exact numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: Year numbers 1–10; horizontal extent 0–12; profit scale 0–4.5 million. Approximate observed heights are 1.2, 1.8, 2.4, 2.25, 2.55, 3.05, 3.2, 3.5, 3.65 and 4 million.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied time series is visible; the trend line and forecast guides are solution-only.

answer.short:
Approximately $\$4\,300\,000$; extrapolation.

Extend a suitable line of best fit to Year 11, beyond the observed Years 1–10.
answer.worked:
Draw an increasing straight line through the middle of the plotted points, with roughly equal numbers above and below. Extend it to Year 11, which represents 1998–1999. A suitable line gives a profit of about $4.3$ million, so the forecast to the nearest $\$100\,000$ is $\$4\,300\,000$.

This is extrapolation because Year 11 lies beyond the observed Years 1–10. Reasonable lines drawn by eye may give slightly different forecasts.

spec.description: Solution-only straight trend line and dashed reading guides, using exactly the question graph's coordinate units and bounding box.
spec.mathematics: One suitable illustrative fit is y=0.3x+1, with y measured in millions; at x=11 it gives y=4.3. The equation is not required student working.
